utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic, and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning. We may resume.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Slokovic-Glumac:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Cilic.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I just point out at the beginning, we looked at the transcript yesterday, and there was some problems because of the speed at which you speak, so please speak as slowly as possible because of the interpreters today, please.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think there was an error regarding the first election results. What were the percentages of the votes won by the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The HDZ won 40.2 per cent of the votes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. That is simply for the sake of correction. You said that you set up a press service, and that within the framework of that press service, you issued a newspaper. After that, a radio station was founded, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what else did you do in the area of the media?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: A local TV station was set up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The radio station on the 17th of April, '92, and the TV station broadcast for the first time on the 17th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you set up these media services, including a TV station?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: From the beginning of the political and national turmoil in the former Yugoslavia, the area of Bosnia and Herzegovina, especially Central Bosnia, inhabited by a large number of Croats, was under total information blockade. We could only receive media from Belgrade and from Sarajevo, which was still absolutely faithful to the official authorities in Belgrade, and we also received newspapers from Belgrade and Sarajevo. There were no newspapers reaching us from Croatia, and the Zagreb radio station could never be received very well in the area of Central Bosnia. Also, the only daily newspaper -- I'm sorry, the only daily news broadcast which we could watch every third day from Zagreb was abolished, and this was something that was very important for us. This was the most important daily news programme at 7.30 p.m. So the Croats felt cut off, that they were receiving information that did not suit their interests but primarily the Serb aggressors and the official policies of the former Yugoslavia and up to an extent also the official authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, apart from the TV Vitez and the Vitez radio station, yourself, did the Muslims have their own local radio and TV station?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At first, when we formed Radio Vitez, representatives of the Muslim people worked with us. This was the press service that I referred to yesterday. They were Midhat Varupa, a lawyer, and Professor Muhamed Halilovic who participated with us on a footing of equality. This went on for two months. However, when we started preparing local TV programmes, Mr. Varupa did participate at first, but in time he ceased coming, so that I must be quite frank and say that the television was, in fact, a Croatian television station because they simply didn't want to participate with us. When they stopped coming to work in Radio Vitez and Radio-Television Vitez, in the part of Stari Vitez which we call Mahala, they set up their own local radio station, which could be compared to ours, though it had a very limited range, it could only cover a part of the Lasva Valley, or even, to be more precise, the municipality of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about their television?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They started with television later. They had a team of journalists and reporters in Mahala, in Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell us, apart from your work in the press service and the radio and TV, did you start working for the army and when?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was only at the beginning of October 1992, at the invitation of a good friend of mine, Mario Cerkez, who at the time was head of the municipal staff of the HVO, who asked me to come and help him in some administrative tasks; and primarily in the area of information, a need was felt already then to provide information for the troops and the members of the municipal staff of the HVO. At the time, I accepted, because I thought this to be both my duty and obligation as a citizen. At the time, when -- the situation was becoming more and more difficult in every respect, the political, national, and economic. So not only because of my feelings of friendship for Mario but also because of my duties as a citizen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the position you held?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was the function of a political officer, it was called. It was assistant commander for political and propaganda activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you there as a professional or were you involved in military affairs?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mario knew very well that there was nothing of the soldier in me. I had no inclination towards the army and towards uniforms, so that I would not have accepted under any circumstances a role which would have had any military aspects to it. But up to an extent, it was military because I was a member of the staff, but operationally, it was a professional duty. I had to prepare reports on the political situation in the municipality of Vitez and beyond and even for the whole area of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a member of the command, were you wearing weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Throughout the war, the war ended, I never had any weapons at all. To be quite frank, in the command there were some other people who didn't carry arms. We had a pistol that three of us would share occasionally. When we would go into the field, we would see whether we might need it. But otherwise, I never carried any weapons, and I was happy that that was so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you need to have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Very often, I would have liked to have one on me because I would cover kilometres where there were no troops and where the lines between the Muslims and Croats were mixed together, but simply there was a shortage of weapons, and a number of members of the command didn't carry them because we thought it was more important for the soldier on the frontline to be armed rather than us in the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I spent the whole war, and it was a bitter winter, and I wore it in a -- I spent it in a camouflage uniform, and in order not to fall ill, I wore all kinds of things over it because this was a summer camouflage uniform. I wore my own jackets and sweaters. I received military boots at the end of the war. Until then, I wore my civilian shoes, even though I spent a lot of time in the field exposed to the snow, the cold, the rain, the wind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, we reached the point when the HVO was set up, first as a municipal staff; that's what you just said.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At the time, it was the municipal staff, and later on, the HVO was officially formed, and then the municipal staff became a part of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were brigades established?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The system of brigades, when talking about the Croats in Vitez, they first became members of a brigade on the 22nd of December, 1992, when the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was formed in Novi Travnik which combined young men from the municipality of Vitez and the municipality of Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The members of that unit coming from the Vitez municipality were members of the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was based in Vitez, but it was part of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade which had another battalion and that was the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was formed together with the Novi Travnik Battalion, were there any other changes prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of changes you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Vitez Battalion separate?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In mid March, the need was felt -- that was the conclusion reached by people of military education -- that one brigade could not function throughout the area and that there was a need for two brigades; and in the middle of March, I don't know the exact date, Stjepan Tomasevic remained in the area of Novi Travnik whereas in the Vitez municipality, the Viteska Brigade was form.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the strength of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number, but prior to the beginning of the war, I think it was about 300 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that the beginning of the war was officially on the 16th of April and the Vitez Brigade was formed in March, how well structured was it, was this brigade, in terms of the troops, the equipment, the training, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Let me try and explain this. We started to build the house from the roof down, the roof being the name of the brigade and the command, whereas everything else was lacking, because if I said that prior to the beginning of the Muslim-Croat conflict, this brigade numbered some 300 men, this is not sufficient even for a battalion, not to mention a brigade, but we called it a brigade maybe also in order to encourage ourselves and perhaps to intimidate our opponents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now give you a list of the members of the 2nd Battalion of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade from February so you will tell us whether this list roughly corresponds and whether the professional indications correspond to what was customarily used to indicate military units.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D18/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, can you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't find my way around very well. For example, the part referring to the command of the 2nd Battalion, my name is not there, and I was a member of the command of that battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible that at the time that all the members of the command were not listed regarding the command staff because the document seems to focus on men rather than positions held in the command. It is more a list of the troops, I think.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It might be because I said at the beginning that my joining the staff was on a professional basis. Maybe that is why I'm not there. But perhaps later on, my name does figure because I was a member, after all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the addresses of the individual soldiers, one can tell that they are mostly soldiers coming from Vitez municipality, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In those days, it was a rarity for anyone outside Vitez municipality to be a member of our units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These numbers, indications of the military post and the date are linked to various units, escort platoon of the 2nd Battalion, et cetera. These names of units, are they correct? Do they correspond to the situation as it was then?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it is -- it is embellished in relation to the real state of affairs. This was a sort of formal structure rather than the actual state of affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the figure of about 300 members, active duty members. Does that correspond?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As from the beginning of 1993 and the beginning of the war the number didn't change significantly, it was within this range of 300 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Up to 300 or more?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I would say up to 300.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Will you please also look at the list of troops of the 1st Battalion, how the villages were represented? This is a document of the Vitez brigade, the 1st Battalion, prior to the conflict, the 14th of April, '93, and we have names by villages -- or, rather, the number of troops provided by each village, and the total number was a target number. So will you look at this and tell us why there is mention of a company? May I call the usher for his assistance, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked D19/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please tell us, in view of the heading of this list, it says, "List of Men of the 1st Battalion by Villages." So it is the 1st Battalion we're talking about. Reviewing these villages, would you say that there were other areas covered by other battalions?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion was the only one that existed, and this is clearly visible from this list of villages, because literally all the larger villages in Vitez municipality are included in this list. There was no 2nd or 3rd Battalion, and that is why I said that the brigade was called the Vitez Brigade, even though by structure it didn't really merit to be called a brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These villages, Nadioci, Santici, Dubravica, Poculica and Rijeka, which part of the 1st Battalion covered these villages?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the eastern part, closer to Busovaca municipality and partly facing Zenica municipality, Mosunj, Mali, Melijke (phoen), Jadun (phoen), Zabilje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is the western part of Travnik municipality, which borders on Travnik and Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this last group, Gornja Verceska, Krcevine, Stari Vitez, Kamenjaca, Gacice?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is a group of villages that are not interconnected. Krcevine is in the northern part of the municipality, closer to Zenica, though there are other Muslim villages behind Krcevine until you reach the boarders of Zenica municipality. Stari Vitez is a part of the urban area around the parish church in Vitez. Kolonjia is the very centre of the town. Kamenjaca is Zabrde where the secondary school centre was, and Gacice is in the southern part of the municipality at the far extreme end in relation to the village of Krcevine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any formal sectors by villages?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. There were four sectors until the moment when the structure was developed to such an extent that we had proper battalions of the Vitez brigade formed later on in the course of the war, but until then the sectors functioned in practice, and they were formed on a territorial principle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the structure of the Vitez brigade completed? When did you have the more or less final list and relatively well-equipped units?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't really think we can talk about proper equipment if we know that for 11 months Vitez was under total information blockade. So we couldn't supply ourselves with the necessary equipment and weapons, but there was mobilisation, additional mobilisation in the course of the war, and I think that in the second half of the war the Vitez brigade was properly structured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the second half? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The late autumn of 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to this list, on 14th of April there were about 260 men who were members of the Vitez brigade, is that correct, this battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Maybe some squads are missing, I don't know if the members of the command staff were there, whether the military police members or maybe there's some soldiers missing, but I don't think that there are many of those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is no Ahmici on this list. Ahmici would probably belong -- if we're looking at the territorial principle, it would belong to the 1st Company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. You see, there were very few Croats in the village of Ahmici. As far as I know, about 15 households in total. And the villages of Nadioci, and Santici, and Dubravica, that is where Ahmici could belong, along with those villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were no active military members in Ahmici if they're not listed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot say there were none, but there were very few. I know most of the people from that area, but there were very few Croats in the Ahmici area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, let me ask you this: If it is not on the list, do you know whether anybody from Ahmici was there? I give you the list. Ahmici is not on the list. Do you know that somebody from Ahmici was there? I only ask you what you know. You don't need to go beyond that. I gave you two lists, so do you know?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, do I not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday we talked something about the co-ordination -- co-ordinating committee for protection of Muslims, and you said that this co-ordinating board -- in fact, I forgot. When was it formed?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This all took place in September, when the Muslim representatives left the municipal government and established a parallel one in a part of Vitez called Mahala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they left the civilian government and the municipal government?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. All positions they were given based on the election results. This all happened in early September, and they formed their own government in Mahala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this co-ordinating board changed its name and became War Presidency at some stage. Do you know when this was?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I could pinpoint the date, but I also believe that it was sometime in the fall. It was either late September or early October, but I know that after they left the municipal government and formed their own government in Mahala, that's when it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The government which was established in Mahala, did it have all agencies, like any other local government?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. And you may ask how I know this. I know it because they were sending their decisions on to our press centre, and my opinion is that they wanted to provide -- to give themselves legitimacy in the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the civilian police? Did they also separate at the same time when the government separated itself?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it was on the same day, but within two or three days, so that by mid-September, in this small area, there was -- we had a situation where the Croatian local government and the Muslim local government functioned side by side and they were really physically separated by only a couple hundred metres, as well as the police and all other agencies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to look at a document, and this is about -- regarding taxes in the new Vitez municipality, and the -- it was going to be realised through the local government in Vitez, and it is signed by Fuad Kaknija.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D20/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Fuad Kaknija's position?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Fuad Kaknija was in a joint government. After the elections he held the same position as here. He was the President of the executive board of the local government and the joint government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what capacity did he adopt this decision to collect taxes with the assistance of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We received this in our press service and commented on it. It ran counter to all -- to the democratic principles, because such a government could not be legitimate, because if we were to start with basic principles, they were in the minority after the elections. And during all the frictions, part of the councilmen from other parties was part of the coalition, but they formed their own government, and you can glean that from this tax collector's office. The budget director, the local communes and all these things, but Fuad Kaknija is still the President of the executive board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when this --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, the interpreters don't have the document to read from. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: There was no translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters have not been provided with the text and counsel is reading from it. It is impossible to follow her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: But afterwards the witness made a statement, so could you translate that? I wonder whether counsel could --

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I don't have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you ask the witness to repeat what he said in response to your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber whether the bodies which I have just enumerated were the structures which are part of the municipal government?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: These structures belong to the municipal authority, and the joint government in Vitez also had the same structures, and after a part of the -- even after the Muslim councilmen left, so all these bodies belong to the government. So now we can discuss its legitimacy. That's a separate issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We also have here that Halid a Munir was charged with implementing all these activities. What is her ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: She is -- he is a Bosnian Muslim, and he was not originally a member of the joint government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was appointed to this new government?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Fuad Kaknija is President of the Executive Board here. He was a member of the original government which was elected after the elections; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. As I just pointed out, I think that this was a way to provide legitimacy to this government in this territory, that is the entire territory of Vitez municipality, and this also means that they would send this to the press outlets and the media outlets like the Radio Vitez. And as far as I know, also -- the taxpayers also received the same type of documents from them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this mean that the councilmen who were given the mandate in the original elections moved their mandate, so to speak, to this new government which was formed in Stari Vitez, given the signature here?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Most all members of government who held certain positions moved to the other government. I'm not sure about the council members, but for the government members, yes, I can say that expressly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given that the government separated and the police separated, this was all in September of '92, did Muslim and Croats continue to work alongside each other in different enterprises, companies or other local services?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Except for the political structures, civilian and military police, there were no other major changes and interruptions of the relationships in the territory of the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether anybody was fired because of the ethnic group to which they belonged?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. We only suffered from the economic hardship, the economic crisis that was there, and I was one victim of this, but many other Croats, Serbs, as well as Bosnian Muslims were victims of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me provide you another document, and I would like you to review it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked D21/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall this document? Was it ever published?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, I have in my notes that this took place -- I remember that this happened at a session I attended, and this is an agreement that was reached then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who attended this meeting? It says the Vitez HVO. It's not very legible. The coordinating board for the protection of Muslims, SDA, and HDZ, and the date is 20 May, 1992. You said that from the signatures you know who these people are.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I know who they are. Ivan Santic, Pero Skopljak for the Croatian side, and Fuad Kaknjo and -- Kajmovic is his last name, he was the SDA member for Vitez, and they represented the Muslims. Fuad Kaknjo was president of this coordinating board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was a member of the war presidency?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, and I believe I know it well, Dr. Muhamed Mujezinovic was president of the war presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this statement, it says, and it is the last paragraph. Can the ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that the Croatian side acknowledged the legality of this coordinating committee?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I will allow that I am maybe biased, but Ivan Santic spent a lot of energy in maintaining the unity in the Vitez municipality, even at the cost of recognising something that was not fully legal. I don't know whether this coordinating body of Muslims in Vitez was seeking to be recognised, but Ivan Santic tried to calm down the situation because the situation was getting more and more critical, and citizens wanted peace, tolerance, and solutions that would benefit everybody in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the municipal building in Old Vitez; do you know where it was?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I know because I went there several times for some meetings. It was in a part called Mahala, it was in the very centre, and it was -- within that complex was the table tennis club, it was -- a fire company was there, it was a local commune, so there was enough space there to organise the agency which was this government, and it was alongside the road which went from Vitez to Travnik, and that is where the police were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will show you another document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked D22/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the heading it says Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Vitez municipality, and War Presidency. It was issued on 11 February, 1993. Does that mean that the war presidency remained until the beginning of war as a separate entity, that is the Muslim ones?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, until the conflict of 16 April, I had no information, and the official Croat government also did not receive any information about any changes, so this war presidency was operational.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given that you were a member of the military structure and you were in the press service, were you receiving such documents; in other words, documents issued by the war presidency?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot say that they were arriving on a regular basis, but the war presidency did try to provide documents to the press service and to Radio Vitez, so we often received their decisions, and it was up to us whether we were going to broadcast them or not. For the most part, we did not give them in raw form; we usually commented on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the seal that they used, the stamp?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and this is the one that was used throughout the period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the seal of the executive board of the Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but again, let me emphasise, it is the Muslim board because it was not the seal that was the seal of the joint government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you have your own seal? You had one with a different coat of arms.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The conclusion is to establish two joint checkpoints of men jointly to control the traffic. In paragraph 2, members of the civilian police of MUP of Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina would man these checkpoints as well as the HVO police, the military police of the BH army, and the HVO military police, and that they would all come to the checkpoints from their own centres. In other words, they never really joined. Because there were some initiatives, they remained separated.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they remained separated throughout, and they never again managed to join together. There were attempts to do so, but -- I have a note. The last attempt to do so was on 27 January, 1993. They tried to reactivate the joint police station in Vitez because it was clear that crime was on the rise. But the attempt failed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that meant that in a small area of Vitez, there were four police agencies?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Civilian police, both Muslim and Croat, and military police, the HVO and the Territorial Defence, which at that time was already the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it also states that all the policemen were going to go to the checkpoints from their own centres. Where were they located?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were in the old police station which was -- the Croat, that is, was in the former Yugoslav police station, and the Muslim one was in Mahala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the military police?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Military police, both the military police units were very close to the civilian police stations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 7 it states that should these conclusions not be implemented, the control checkpoints would have to be established in a different way, and the 3rd Corps of the BH army was going to be responsible for it. Did you take this as a threat?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You could understand it in different ways. You can understand it as if the HVO was not legitimate, that the only legitimate formations in this area were the BH army units, in this case the 3rd Army Corps, because the area of Vitez was, according to them, part of the 3rd Corps territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is also stated that all local village checkpoints in Vitez municipality should be abolished.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters do not have copies of these documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did these checkpoints appear?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They mushroomed, literally. Wherever anybody thought it would be a good idea to have a checkpoint, there was a checkpoint, and virtually on all roads and crossroads, points leading into town and out of town and into villages and sometimes also in various other places throughout the Lasva River Valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the Muslims usually set up their checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They had a checkpoint at the entrance and exit to Mahala; this is on the main road running through the urban part of Vitez. Later on, agreement was reached to remove this checkpoint, but these agreements never lasted. They would be removed, and a day or two later, they would crop up again. Also, checkpoints would be put up on a road leading from the centre of town to the Vitezit factory, a road used by many workers who experienced all kinds of unpleasantness at these informal checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there checkpoints at Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At Kruscica, very frequently there were checkpoints, but in my view, there's a very serious reason for this. In the southern part of Kruscica, outside the settlement itself, HVO members were quartered into motels, whereas a part of the village behind the motels were inhabited by a majority Muslim population, and therefore, in a part of Kruscica which separates the Croatian from the Muslim part, at a locality known as Fatina Vodica, they would set up a checkpoint where several incidents occurred, seizure of weapons, vehicles, and even exchange of fire, and the arrest of a number of members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, but I am unable to find a particular document because this witness came earlier than we had originally planned. We will come back to that topic later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Grbavica, please?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: An important part of the Vitez-Travnik road or the ring road around Vitez which links up with the road from Vitez at a point called Grbavica was a place where a checkpoint was frequently put up, and numerous incidents occurred there, and perhaps later on during my testimony we will see that this was one of the reasons for the conflict in Vitez municipality. I can also say without you reminding me that there were checkpoints often on the road going from Vitez across the pass at Vjetrenice to Zenica, then there were checkpoints also on the road from Bila towards Zenica, and the Catholic Zupa, Brajkovici, and further on to Zenica, then in settlements with a Muslim majority population such as Sadovace and Han Bila, and there were many misunderstandings and clashes that occurred at these checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please examine another document? It is an announcement of the civilian government of the Vitez HVO. It has to do with the problems of the accommodation of the army and the police in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D23/2.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could a copy be placed on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I wonder whether a spare copy could be placed on the ELMO at the request of the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Have you got a spare copy?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: No. I have a problem with this set of documents. I just don't have enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Therefore, may I ask you to read slowly, if you read from this document, so that the interpreters can follow it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is an announcement of the civilian government at an extraordinary session held on the 2nd of January, 1993, which says that the government reviewed the security and political situation in the municipality resulting from the concentration of numerous heterogeneous military institutions in Vitez and the most recent incidents during the Christmas and New Year holidays. It was noted that in Vitez at present, the following have been accommodated: the regional staff of the HVO, the staff of the regional military police of the HVO, the staff of the Vitez Battalion of the HVO, the municipal military police of the HVO, the municipal civilian police, the barracks of the armed forces in Kruscica, the armed forces barracks in Preocica, the municipal headquarters of the armed forces of Vitez, the municipal military police of the armed forces of Vitez within the framework of which there is the civilian Muslim police and barracks housing the special unit Vitezovi in the Dubravica school. The heterogeneity of various and sometimes contradictory interests of the mentioned institutions, which all find themselves in a narrow area, increasingly provoke undesirable incidents with sometimes tragic consequences. The HVO government of Vitez has reviewed this problem at its session held on the 28th of December, 1992, and in connection with the accommodation of the HVO troops and the troops of the armed forces has expressed a very definite position that all the troops and all the headquarters should be accommodated in the barracks in Travnik, Zenica, Busovaca, and Kiseljak, and that schools and hotels should be vacated. Reference is also made to uncontrolled shooting during the Christmas and New Year holidays on a large scale and the death of military policeman Mate Jakovljevic on the 1st of January, 1993, which have made an unfavourable situation critical. In view of these developments in Vitez, the impression is that a conflict of larger proportions could break out at any moment which would call in question the lives of policemen, troops, commanders, and even neutral citizens. It was also noted that the military is, on a daily basis and in various ways, provoking unnecessary material damage. It is our view that preventive measures need to be taken urgently. The Vitez HVO government continues to uphold the view that the troops and their commands, both of the HVO and of the armed forces, OS, should be accommodated in two barracks. After the latest developments, we insist on the same for the regional military police. Signed by the President of the Vitez HVO, Ivan Santic. Mr. Cilic, do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember this communiqué? Was this a problem that was discussed on several occasions?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, indeed it was, and as far as I can remember, attempts were made through the regional headquarters of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia and the 3rd Corps in Zenica to implement such a decision. However, these proposals on the part of the government did not meet with understanding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When reference is made to the armed forces in Kruscica, Preocica, the municipal staff of the armed forces, the municipal military police of the armed forces, whose army is that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All this refers to the Muslim forces of the civilian and military police, and the troops themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they use the expression "armed forces" before they became the BH army?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They used term "Territorial Defence," but in certain situations they also used the term "the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were units and commands ever moved in response to this proposal?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, no, everything remained the same as it was prior to this request on the part of the HVO government in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. With the help of the usher, I should like to distribute another document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D24/2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, my colleague Radovic asks for permission to be excused for a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document of the Defence headquarters of the district of Zenica, dated the 13th of November, 1992, and the subject is securing accommodation for units of the armed forces of the republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is addressed to the command in Vitez, signed --

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, it seems to me that the English translation that we have does not correspond to the document in the Croatian language. This is a document signed by Mr. Merdan, and we're not quite sure that we have the right translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: It's the 13th of November. It's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: It's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: It's okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you looked at this document?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you read the contents? Let me read a part that I should like to ask you to comment on, "Based on the order of the headquarters of the supreme command of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, strictly confidential, dated 4th July," we can't see the year, "On the formation of commands, staffs and units of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, with the aim of taking action in time for accommodation into barracks and for passing the winter there, I order immediately take action with the competent authorities in the municipality to secure accommodation facilities in constructed buildings for command staffs and units, which are being formed, on the basis of the above-quoted order. The facilities and deployment of units in them should be performed according to the plan of use. The facilities need to be furbished and plans of safety drawn up." Paragraph 3, "The organisation should be set in such a way that within the framework of battalions and units, and thereby also for the commands and lower units, food should be provided and distributed." And final paragraph, "Take all other actions you consider indispensable which will contribute to the best possible conditions of life, work and combat of your units. Report to this command of action taken in this area. Be extremely persistent in executing this order, and insist with the authorities that they carry out their part of the work." So obviously this concerns the deployment of units of the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as they are called in this document, in Vitez. The Vitez command covered Vitez and the surrounding villages; didn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could such a document circulate freely. Would it be possible to conceal the accommodation of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You're asking me whether this document was concealed. I'm not sure that it was. Regardless of the fact that it has the indication, "Strictly confidential," I think it was something that was well-known to the public at large, because the Vitez municipality's too small an area for any activities to prepare the construction of buildings and for the stationing of military units to be carried out without the public knowing about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were such buildings built in the area of Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were not, but the existing buildings were improved and refurbished because there was a shortage of funds for the construction of new buildings. So in Vitez most of the existing buildings were used for this purpose. For instance, in Preocica, Bukve, Kruscica the existing school buildings were used, because the schools were not working at the time, there was no -- there were no courses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says here that in addition to construction work, security plans need to be drafted. What does that mean, according to your military knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It means that the surrounding area needs to be secured, because it is logical if you put a unit -- accommodate a unit in a particular building to spend the winter there, then the surrounding area has to have security provided to prevent any surprises, because tension by then was running high between the Muslims and Croats, and, therefore, also between the BH army and the HVO. And in the immediate vicinity -- or, rather, not so far away were units of the Yugoslav People's Army or the Serb forces by then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this document is intended partly to plan for logistic support; doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. We can see from this that serious efforts were made to structure units belonging to the Muslim people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the testimony so far, we have already heard that there were no barracks, but here in the third paragraph reference is made to the need for food to be prepared for commands and lower units. Does that mean that there were people grouped in large numbers? Were barracks used?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In Travnik, for instance, the barracks were used, but in other cases other existing facilities were adapted for use as barracks, and this was the widespread practice in this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: May we distribute this document as well, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked D25/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document issued by Ivan Santic, the President of the HVO government in Vitez, on the 28th of December, 1992, refers to what you have just said. I will read out part of this document. "Regarding the accommodation of HVO forces and forces -- and the armed forces, the HVO government has taken a very explicit position. The army and the command should be moved to the barracks in Travnik, Zenica, Busovaca and Kiseljak, and the schools and hotels should be vacated." The last paragraph says, "The military units of the BH armed forces are placed in the regional schools in Preocica, and Kruscica and in private houses owned by Mr. Miso Andric in Kruscica. A large number of soldiers have been accommodated, which is preventing the beginning of the school year, and at the same time this contributes significantly to growing interethnic tension. A parallel civil police is being formed, as well as a Muslim TV. All that is done in practice is leading to even greater rifts between these two peoples, even though the official policy of Mr. Izetbegovic pays lip-service to togetherness." And on page 2 it says, "We propose that a meeting be urgently organised in which the following should participate: The commander of the regional HVO command, the commander of the regional headquarters of the BH armed forces, the head of the defence office in the government of Vitez, the commander of the municipal staff of the armed forces of Vitez" -- this is missing in the translation -- "chairman of the coordination committee for the protection of Muslims in Vitez, and chairman of the temporary civil HVO war government of Vitez." So this refers to all the things that you have mentioned regarding problems with the accommodation of troops in schools, and that it was difficult for schools to start working and for civilian life to be organised. So this is a document dated the 28th of December, 1992, and all these bodies referred to here, that is both military HVO bodies, and on the other hand, the bodies of the armed forces, then the civilian bodies of the HVO and the civilian body of the coordination committee of the Muslim government, at the time all of these are co-existing in Vitez, with the exception of the regional command of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think this may be an error. This was the municipal command, not the regional command, but all the others were functioning within the territory of Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were aware of these problems, in view of your activities in the press service, and also as a member of the command of the Vitez brigade, did you receive complaints of this kind from the government?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, or I was personally present at government meetings, or alternatively, I would get the conclusions from those meetings in writing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this problem did crop up on a number of occasions and attempts were made to deal with it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I think this was a problem that appeared on the agenda of each meeting of the government in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. So we'll take now a 20-minute break. We'll reconvene at 10.50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mrs. Slokovic-Glumac, before you start, I should tell Defence counsel and the Prosecution that I have just had a meeting with the Deputy Registrar and the head of the division on translation and interpretation, and they, of course, conveyed to me the worries of the interpreters. We have excellent interpreters, but in spite of that, of course, they are not able to follow if they are not provided with a copy of the documents. So I would like to make an appeal, first of all, to give the interpreters the documents in the original and possibly also the English translation anytime a document is tendered in evidence; and secondly, also, to slow down, because, you know, the transcript is in English, and if we miss most of the words because of the quick pace of what is being said, then, of course, this means that the Court will base itself on a transcript which is not absolutely accurate, and this is not the fault of the interpreters or the stenotypists or stenographers but only because of the excessive velocity of the pace. So if you can slow down, also I hope the witness will slow down, and also you wait a few seconds before you ask a question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I can give copies of the documents now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: If it is possible, I can give the copies of the documents now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, please. Yes. And also one final point: The Deputy Registrar, Mr. Heintz, is suggesting that there should be a meeting of all Defence counsel with him and the head of the interpretation division possibly on Thursday when we are not holding any hearing so that you can have an exchange of views about the question of interpretation and so on. This is for the sake of accuracy in our transcript. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: This is a set of the documents I am going to use during this next hour, so I can give it to the usher for the interpretation unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more time, good morning, Mr. Cilic.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will now review another document of 27 January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D26/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document which was compiled during the meeting between UNHCR representatives, UNPROFOR, SDA party, BH army, the HVO government, the HVO headquarters, and public security station in Vitez. In the body of text, under 2: A joint police station is to be reactivated in Vitez. The structure of the employees will be ethnically balanced. Given the specific conditions at the moment, the police station will work according to the rules which are to be agreed on at a level of Vitez municipality government. Mr. Mirko Samija and Mr. Saban Mahmutovic are in charge of implementation of this assignment which shall be carried out immediately. Item 3, in order to overcome the current problems in the Vitez municipality, a temporary municipal war government will be established which shall be ethnically balanced. Ivan Santic, Fuad Kaknjo, Dragan Rados, and Midhat Varupa will make a proposal within five days of this meeting. Number 4, commanders of the HVO Brigade, Mr. Mario Cerkez and Mr. Esad Dzenanovic of the BH army shall proceed with an exchange of prisoners and goods and they will remove the illegally set up checkpoints. From this document, we can see that attempts were continually made to re-establish the joint police station and joint government.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of these attempts, and attempts were made continuously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The composition of attendees at this meeting and those who tried to re-establish the joint government are Ivan Santic, Dragan Rados, Fuad Kaknjo, and Midhat Varupa.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: These four persons were all members of the initial government. Ivan Santic and Dragan Rados are ethnic Croats and Fuad Kaknjo and Midhat Varupa are ethnic Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall, in item 4, it is said that an immediate exchange of prisoners was to take place as well as confiscated goods. Do you know what kind of exchange it was?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that one of the main reasons for this meeting was an incident which took place in the area called Kruscica. On that day, at the checkpoint which is called Fatina Vodica, which is in Kruscica, members of the BH army disarmed and arrested HVO soldiers who were coming back to Vitez after they were relieved of duty, and they were deployed there in that area of Kruscica where there were some logistics facilities of the HVO. I don't know the exact number, but I think that there were ten or twelve. They were taken prisoner, they were disarmed and then taken, and the members of the BH army took them away. So this is why I believe that partly this meeting, which had been planned earlier, was then held immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also, it is mentioned to dismantle the illegal checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This was a constant problem, and with the Court's permission, let me add something that may not be strictly part of your question, but I remember this meeting very well and this situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At a meeting, agreement was reached in principle to make the joint government and police jointly and to rename it the war presidency and war government of Vitez. The Croatian side accepted it, and it requested of the Muslims to create an oasis of peace in this area of Bosnia, of Central Bosnia, and this government would work by using both seals. This was not strictly legal, but the Croatian side accepted this. So that the documents going to the Croatian side would bear a Croatian seal and those documents that would go, let's say, to Zenica or Sarajevo, would be stamped with the Muslim seal, and those documents which would go to international organisations would have both seals. This was to be a piece of cunning, so to speak, on the part of both Croatian and Muslim sides in Vitez to keep the peace and to also satisfy the needs of both Croatian and Muslim governments in Vitez and also to make it satisfactory for the International Community. However, I have to say that this was never implemented even though this was agreed on at this meeting of 27 January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the municipal war government which is mentioned in item 3, it was not called Croatian or HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it was literally called Vitez Municipality - The Municipal War Government of Vitez. So it was ethnically neutral.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. In connection with what you have just said regarding this meeting, that it was held because of the capture and disarming of a group of soldiers in Kruscica, the HVO soldiers, that is, in that connection, I would like you to look at another document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D27/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is with respect to that incident of 27 January, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means on 27 January, 1993, in Kruscica, near Fatina Vodica and the fire station in Stari Vitez, the following materiel and technical equipment were confiscated by the BH army. 1. A TAM minibus, licence plate TR 283-12. Further, were any weapons taken from the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. The weapons are usually the first thing that are taken, and they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regarding the weapons, can the witness please be shown the following document? Sorry. Can we have the usher's assistance?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D28/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is also a report of 27 January, 1993, which was compiled by Ivan Budimir, security officer. Do you know Ivan Budimir?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. He was my good friend. Unfortunately, he is no longer alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise his signature?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise his signature, I know him, and I'm sorry that he is no longer alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the body of text, it says that on 27 January, 1993, in Kruscica, a regular shift change was carried out. On the way back from Kruscica, a TAM minibus van, licence plate TR 283-12, was stopped at 1230 hours. It was driven by Stipo Livancic who was driving all the members of the shift. All occupants of the vehicle were disarmed and the minibus was confiscated. The following weapons were confiscated: four pieces of Kalashnikov rifles, one light machine gun, three pieces of Thompson automatic rifle, five pieces of Sokac, one piece of semi-automatic rifle, two M-48 rifles, one pistol, another pistol, hand grenades, 15 pieces. Do you recall whether these weapons were returned?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I remember very well the whole situation. The minibus was returned, and the weapons, despite negotiations which went on for several days, were never returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These were the weapons that had been carried by the people who had been stopped and detained?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: For a while, they were detained in a room which was controlled by the BH army soldiers. However, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic and members of the Viteska Brigade and the civilian authorities and through contacts with the Muslim authorities and the armed forces, the soldiers were released fairly quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the Viteska Battalion was deployed in Kruscica, that is, members of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they accommodated?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were accommodated in two motels called Lovac and Plavac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people are we talking here?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that the whole shift consisted of about 15 men. That is based on the list that you have also just provided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further along in the body of text, it says that the following weapons were confiscated from the regional policemen in the course of the day, and these policemen were Zlatko Ivankovic, Ilija Santic, and Mijo Dzotle: 7.62 millimetre Ciganka automatic rifle, two pieces; one Kalashnikov automatic rifle; one Zbrojovka pistol, one pistol, and 150 Deutschmarks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I don't think it is necessary for you to read it out because everybody has a copy of this document, so for the sake of time, you could simply ask questions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall that event?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall, because on 27 January, 1993, when the incident in Kruscica took place, in the morning we knew that another checkpoint in Mahala had been set up because this is Stari Vitez, that is Gornji Vitez, Upper Vitez, this is an area also known as Mahala, where their local government, the armed forces headquarters and the military police were all set up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further on, Drago Sliskovic from the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade command and was stopped at this checkpoint and weapons were also received from him. This was a member of the brigade command. Do you recall that incident? And it was the same day.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember it, because this was a colleague and acquaintance of mine who was in the same brigade. Except for these two incidents, there were additional incidents, a total of about 15 incidents on that day, and I think that here just the major ones were listed here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All this was on 27 January?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. And the reason for this incident on 27 January was because the schools which had a Croatian curriculum had stopped working on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the checkpoint near the fire station Pero Petrovic's weapons, a sniper rifle and a pistol, were also seized. That was -- the fire station was also in -- of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. They were right next to these centres of Muslim government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further on it says that two radio sets were also seized from Mario Garic and Zoran Jukic, as well as a pistol, and a vehicle was seized by Zeljo Karin. Do you recall whether the vehicle was returned?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The vehicle was returned but not the radio transmitters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The contents of this report which is marked D27, which is about seizure of weapons, also lists the names of some persons from whom these weapons were seized, and it also mentions that a certain amount of ammunition was taken from these people, as well as some personal effects. Will you please look an at these -- at this document under 6?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Do I not have this document in front of me. The gentleman has taken it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please look at it again? Do you know any of the people listed?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: More or less all of them, including the driver of the mini-bus and the owner of that mini-bus, who is still operating this service. Yes, they were members of our units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the large number of incidents that occurred at the checkpoints over a certain period of time, what was the security situation regarding the citizens of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The security situation for all citizens in Vitez was below any acceptable standards, which means it was very, very poor. In fact, people moved only in extreme necessity, in the evening and at night, because there were so many people under arms moving around in the municipality, belonging to all kinds of units, formal and informal ones. Alcohol was consumed excessively. There were groups prone to plunder, destruction, devastation, so that the situation was alarming, to put it mildly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When talking about citizens, you are implying both Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I mean all the citizens of Vitez, because at the time people had still not been evicted from their homes, nor had they moved from their houses, with the exception of a certain number of Serbs who had left the municipality of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the reasons for this situation? You mentioned alcohol, the abundance of weapons. What about the refugees coming in?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were refugees and their troubles also added to our own troubles, because there was a large concentration of exiled people, Muslims, in the first place, coming from the area of Western Bosnia, which at the time were fully under the occupation of the Yugoslav People's Army, or better still, of the local Serbs, that is the Bosnian Serbs. And this large concentration of refugees existed in Central Bosnia, whereas the exiled Croats from those regions abandoned Central Bosnia and looked for places with greater safety. They used the Central Bosnia in transit, and they went towards the south of Bosnia-Herzegovina where there was a much larger concentration and share of Croats in the total population, and they went to Croatia and also further on to other European countries where many of them had relatives and friends, whereas the Muslims mostly stayed on in the area of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was that situation affected by the fact that a large -- an enormous amount of arms were circulating?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Simply things were out of control. There was black marketeering in weapons so one could buy weapons even from the Serbs on the frontlines. Then there were certain underground channels along which weapons were sold. And individuals helped people, and it was impossible to make sure those people were physically and mentally capable of carrying arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The army, or, rather, the HVO and the military police of the HVO, did they attempt to establish some kind of law and order?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Attempts were made repeatedly, and I remember numerous orders coming from the Operative Zone command, through the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade command and later on the Vitez Brigade command, instructing certain services within the army and the military police, in the first place, to control the peace and to try and establish at least a minimum degree of law and order in Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the civilian police operating?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was just going to say that, that there was the civilian police as well, as well as the municipal authorities who sought in every possible way to maintain law and order, because this situation put the citizens in a very difficult position, and many of them sought ways to abandon the area. I think it was in January that the municipal government, the Croatian government in Vitez, took the decision to form an intervention squad. This intervention squad was composed of selected young men who had been tested in terms of their morals and also physically, they were mentally in good health, they had no criminal record, and they were ready to intervene physically and with force of arms to maintain law and order. A decision was even taken that they should have certain compensation. At the time it was quite considerable, because salaries were very low, whereas I think the members of the squad received up to 400 or 500 German marks, which was an extremely high salary for a month. For comparison's sake, the regular salaries in enterprises were about 50 marks. Heading this intervention squad was an individual, an exceptional individual in every sense of the word. He was called Kreso Garic, and I think this intervention's platoon achieved enviable results, at least in the town, urban area itself. It restored peace and security to a level that could be tolerated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was responsible for inside inspections for arrests, for the initiation of criminal proceedings in relation to the members of the army? Was this done by the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I will be able to answer this question of yours, but I don't think that the civilian police could interfere with any act that involved a military person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another question: You said that the civilian police was functioning but still an intervention squad had to be formed to restore order, which means that it wasn't functioning.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It wasn't functioning. It didn't have the strength nor the power. I just found the date that this intervention squad was formed, on the 25th of February, and it was operative until the conflict escalated on the 16th of April, '93.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here is another announcement for the public, so will you please look at it and tell me whether you remember it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D29/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document of the Croatian Defence Council of Novi Travnik, number 12/93. It was compiled on behalf of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade. I can't see the signature?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it must have been Pero Jurisic, so please take that under reservation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall this event?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do very well, because it was a typical one, and as we were told in the press service, by HVO representatives from Novi Travnik and which was supported by Colonel Blaskic, this was meant to be a warning to everyone that no such incidents would be tolerated against the Muslim people. There would be no leniency for any representative of the Croats, regardless of the fact whether he was a member of the HVO, a policeman or a civilian, if he physically attacked or stole from a Muslim. The aim was to try and contain violence regardless of who the victim may be, a Muslim, a Croat or a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it says here that Zoran Jukic, known as Juka, from Novi Travnik was killed when resisting efforts of the Novi Travnik HVO military police to bring him into custody for harassing and seriously wounding a Muslim citizen. Did you publish this report?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We broadcast it, and I can tell you that the investigation about this murder and this incident was completed post-haste, and the people who killed this person were acquitted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To clarify this, Zoran Jukic was a Croat?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and the Croatian policemen who shot him were also Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please look at another document now?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D30/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, the 2nd Battalion, a document compiled by Ivan Budimi, the officer of security and information. The document says that groups and individuals wearing uniforms and with HVO insignia are plundering socially and more often privately owned property. During the robberies they use all the methods of criminals. Then it goes on to say that their main objective is to loot. However, no effort is being made to put an end to this, their criminal offences put additional strain on the already tense interethnic relations. Then several examples are given. We can see that individual members of the HVO were arrested while looting houses, committing robbery in a state of intoxication, aggravated robbery, and those names are listed there. Were attempts made to put an end to crime within HVO ranks?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that very resolute measures were taken, but in view of the situation in which we were living when we were surrounded with so many soldiers, units that were out of control, people who, wearing uniforms and insignia, committed criminal offences, better results could not have been expected in spite of the resolute measures taken. I think that Colonel Tihomir Blaskic insisted in particularly on law and order and discipline among members of the HVO, because only then could the citizens trust this army, because if the army commits misdeeds and robberies, then it cannot be considered to belong to any people. However, the results could not be satisfactory for the citizens of Vitez or the surroundings, because these criminal activities were quite well organised, and this applies in particular to certain groups of criminals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In conclusion, it is stated that resolute steps should be taken to stop these occurrences, particularly because of interethnic relations. Are you aware of further instructions given to the Vitez brigade as to how they should behave and whether proceedings were taken against those who perpetrated criminal acts within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I must comment on this.
