Mr. Ivan Budimir addressed a similar document to the Bosniak side, because there were occasions of criminals joining ranks on both sides, that's Croats and Muslim criminals acting together, and he wanted both the civilian and military authorities to act jointly to suppress crime. At the same time, we were trying to find a way to prevent members of our units committing criminal acts, and one of the measures taken was the prohibition on carrying weapons in town, the prohibition on wearing uniforms when people were not on duty, and some other measures were taken. Of course, some of these measures did have a positive effect, but as I said, not sufficiently so to satisfy the citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The persons mentioned here, there are several names. They are all Croats and they're all HVO members?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Proceedings -- summary proceedings were taken against them. Many of them ended up in the prison in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more document linked to this same area.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D31/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is another report of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, 2nd Battalion, the Viteska, the Vitez Battalion, on the 22nd of January, 1993, compiled by Ivan Budimir, and referring to some incidents, such as throwing of explosive devices in town in the zone of responsibility of the 2nd Battalion. Were such occurrences frequent and were any attempts made to prevent them?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were very frequent, and that is perhaps the reason why, out of all these mentioned, I can only remember the shell thrown into Zoran Krizanovic's apartment in the centre of town, because these other incidents referred to here did not have more serious consequences, and that is probably the reason why I haven't memorised them, because there were dozens and dozens of them occurring on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you do not know who the damaged parties were; it is just stated that these devices were thrown at certain public places, the Red Cross building, the civilian MUP.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You see, one can conclude from this what the intention was. The Red Cross building in the centre of Vitez was under the control of the Croats. The health clinic was already functioning on an ethnic basis because the Muslims had their own health centre in Mahala. The civilian MUP is in the centre of town, a building right next to the headquarters of the municipal government. At the time, only Croatian policemen were there. Also, the apartment of Zoran Krizanovic, which was hit with a hand-held rocket launcher, he was a Croat, and this was in the centre of town. The perpetrators were not discovered, so one cannot explicitly claim who they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were such incidents of which both Muslims and Croats were victims?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. There were incidents all over Vitez, it was chaotic, and one could not attribute them to ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Bosniak police carry out on-site investigations when any such act was perpetrated?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Any crime or incident that occurred, attempts were made to coordinate the investigations and to prevent such criminal acts, so that certain points were controlled by the HVO, others by the Muslims, and others by both of them together. But obviously, both within the police and military ranks, there were criminals whose interests were furthered by this widespread crime. To what extent the Bosniak side sought to prevent crime, I really don't know. I don't have the necessary information to tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask you whether you perhaps remember the killing of Bernard Kovacevic and Ivan Laus in the village of Cajdras at the military police checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that this happened, I didn't know those young men, but the incident resounded throughout Central Bosnia, and all the media commented on it, of course differently and each in its own way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these were members of the HVO military police of the Jure Francetic Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is a Croatian police unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are moving on to 19 October, 1992. At that time, you were the acting chief at the HVO brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was in the command staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And where were you sent?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Fifteen days after I joined the command as a political officer, on orders of Colonel Tihomir Blaskic which went through the municipal staff and other staffs, Mario Cerkez, the chief of staff, I was sent on this date, 19 October, to a seminar in Busovaca which was organised by the representatives of the Red Cross in Geneva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the topic of this seminar?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This seminar was held for the representatives of the HVO, and as I found out -- and this was a full-day seminar; a similar one had been also organised for the representatives of the BH army, and the topic of the seminar was the International Conventions on the Laws of War. We received a lot of promotional material in English and Croatian. We also saw films on the activities of the Red Cross, and many of us, for the first time, learned more about the history of the Red Cross and its goals and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this seminar also include a discussion of the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It was about the rights of prisoners, about the rights of prisoners of war, and I have to say that this seminar left a great impression on me. I asked myself, why are they showing us this? because they were showing us a number of films from countries in Africa, South America, and they were very disturbing images.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you thought that this could not happen in your region?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I thought that it was very far removed, and I thought that it could never happen in our country. But we received a lot of materials, and I distributed it to our soldiers, all these instructions, and to the commanding officers. I thought that they would never be used, but it turned out that they were quite needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, you went back to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The seminar finished between 3.00 and 3.30, and in my car, I started back home. It's about 12 kilometres. But about four kilometres down the road, I was stopped because there was a backup. I stopped my car and I came out and asked what was going on, and they said that there was a traffic accident. Then I parked on the shoulder of the road and I started walking home, and the backup of vehicles was about 300 metres. I arrived at the site of the accident, and I was told that three people were killed in this accident from Bila, this is in the Vitez municipality, and also another person was seriously injured. My friend, the public prosecutor, Vlado Miskovic, was present on site. He is now a federal prosecutor, that is in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. While he was doing the on-site investigation, he asked me how I was going to proceed to Vitez, and I told him that I had a car, and then he said, "But don't you know that a barricade had been set up in Ahmici, a barricade set up by the BH army members, and that road is blocked?" I told him that I did not know, and I was almost in a panic, I was very tired, I was hungry, I didn't know how I was going to get back home because there were no other ways to get home. Then with Vlado Miskovic, I decided to take a liberty and pass the entire column and join him. He was there escorted by the civilian police. So I did so. I went back to my car, and in the car, I joined them. A number of drivers who were also waiting to pass reacted very noisily at this liberty, this licence I took. However, I just proceeded and joined the vehicle of the public prosecutor, and then we proceeded. From there to the point where the barricade had been set up was another 1.5 kilometres, and there we were stopped by -- we were stopped, both vehicles, the public prosecutor's vehicle and his police escort vehicle were stopped, and I stopped as the third vehicle. There were about 15 soldiers which were armed to the teeth, and they were on the road and in the Catholic cemetery which was adjoining the road. Part of the concrete fence had been broken down and a machine gun was set up inside the cemetery. Now, this was a winter day and dusk was falling. However, I could see the soldiers and this machine gun nest because it had not gotten that dark that I could not recognise the faces of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also see trenches to the right of the road?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, there was a group of four or five soldiers. There was also some shrubbery there. I didn't look very much. I didn't want to provoke them by peering in that direction. However, this part of the cemetery was right in front of me because there is a curve in the road, and as I stopped, as I pulled to a stop, I saw those soldiers and those who were right in front of me because they were right there at the curve and at the top of the Catholic cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the barricade, the barrier, made of?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was something that was -- that used to be called hedgehog, which is a contraption made out of iron bars which prevents vehicles, even heavy vehicles, from passing. A vehicle can pass only if one of these hedgehogs is removed. In addition to these soldiers and these hedgehogs, there were several anti-tank mines, and I had enough military knowledge, having served in the military in my own day, that there were no other barriers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were let through.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When the police vehicle which was escorting the public prosecutor was let through and the team of investigators, then my turn came, and they took my documents, and when the policeman asked me to open the trunk of my car, one member of the group from the cemetery said loudly enough so that I could hear him, "Let him through. I know him." So there was no further control of me, and I was let through and allowed to proceed to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the way to Vitez, did you notice anything unusual?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: By the time I arrived in Vitez, it was completely dark. I live in a part of Vitez which later on became the frontline between the Croatian and Bosnian side, Mahala, and I had a garage where I kept my car another 150 metres farther away towards the town. This was sort of the demarcation zone between us and the Muslims. So I had a habit of parking and then going to the command staff, and I did so in order to report on what I did at the seminar. However, when I approached the garage that night, I pulled my car to a stop, and I heard some noises, some noises that sounded like weapons, and somebody said, "Stop. Don't budge." So I said, "I'm not budging." And they said, "What do you want? What are you doing here?" And I said, "It's my garage here. I'm trying to leave the car there."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose army was it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I could not see them, but based on the location, they could only have been members of the BH army because where they were standing was already the territory which unofficially was under their control. However, as I assumed that these were young men who knew me because we were neighbours, then I was allowed to park the car in my garage and I was not bothered, I was allowed to go back home, and this was another distance 400 metres in total.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next in Vitez, that is, in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That night, after I put my car in the garage, when I went to the command post, the commander, Mario Cerkez, told me that a similar checkpoint was also set up in Grbavica, near the construction company Bosna. This is an intersection where the transit roads -- a detour is around the town of Vitez and the road proceeds to Travnik. However, Mario also told me that there were intense negotiations going on between the BH army and the HVO, civilian authorities of both sides, and that the representatives of UNPROFOR and UNHCR were mediating these negotiations. However, I was told to go home and rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other incidents with respect to the HVO and the BH army, conflicts?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the conflicts escalated the next day because the negotiations did not produce any results, and so the police units and HVO unit which was on its way to Jajce, which at that time was in a critical situation because it was surrounded by the Serbian forces, they smashed this barricade. They physically dismantled the barricade in Ahmici. This was a very fierce conflict, and later I learned that this checkpoint in Ahmici was reinforced by other forces, so there weren't 15 people any longer. In some estimates, there were up -- and in my view, there was up to 50 people there, and there was a fierce conflict, but fortunately, there were very few people injured. And near the village of Grbavica, the BH army members dismantled the barricade themselves, so there was no conflict there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But members of the Viteska Brigade did take part in the physical dismantling of this barricade?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, we were not tasked with doing so. It was the military police of the HVO which was involved in dismantling this barricade, assisted by members of the unit which was going to Jajce from Busovaca and Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the village watches involved in this dismantling?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. They had a different role. They did not even appear or they did not have any role in this. They could not have had any role because their weapons were very primitive, they did not have equipment, and so it was not possible for them to take part in this conflict of that size, and this was the first serious conflict between the BH army and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the blockade of the command post of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do know, because at that same time, while an attempt was being made to lift the blockade of this communication line near Ahmici, members of the Vitezovi Brigade also blocked the Territorial Defence headquarters in Vitez, and members of the BH army blocked the regional staff of the HVO in Kruscica, that is, which was in the lawless (phoen) facility, so those two command posts were blocked, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So de facto this was the operational zone headquarters.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, even though it was not called that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Kruscica? That was a dominant position, right?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. That was where the headquarters of the operational zone was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We will take now a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Slokovic-Glumac, before you resume your examination-in-chief we have a query. We are wondering why you're not sticking to the chronological order, because we went up to April -- sorry, January/February '93 and now we're going back to October '92. Is there a reason for that or do you intend to follow an order that is not chronological in your questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: No, but what happened was that I tried to group the problems for the Court, so I selected groups of documents. That was more of an introduction. Now I will be going on to more specific events linked to the indictment, and these are elements which I feel that the Prosecution has also referred to in his case, although in a different manner. So this is more of a background rather than any chronological order of events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, we broke off when you said that the HVO command was blocked, that is the regional command in Kruscica and the TO in the secondary school centre in Vitez. How was this problem resolved; do you know?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was resolved by lifting the blockade of the regional headquarters at Lovac, as well as the TO headquarters in the secondary school, and then the TO staff abandoned the secondary school and moved to Stari Vitez and was based there in the part known as Mahala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened with the regional HVO headquarters? Did it move?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: After that, I don't exactly remember how much after, a day or two after, it also moved to the hotel in Vitez. Perhaps it is worth mentioning that a very important incident occurred also on the 20th at the crossed roads between Dolac and the road leading to Guca Gora, when Ivica Stojak, an HVO commander was killed. Members of the BH army shot at him in the back. They had a checkpoint there on the road between Travnik and Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: May I ask the usher for his assistance to distribute this document so that the witness can look at it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D32/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says an announcement issued on the 22nd of October, 1992 in the presence of the UNHCR and UNPROFOR, and representatives of the armed forces of Vitez, the HVO, the HVO headquarters and representatives of religious communities, Father Anto Tomas and Omer Efendija Mestrovac. And the agreement was that all remaining barricades in Vitez municipality should be removed, and primarily at Kruscica and the crossroads with the road leading to Zenica. Who held the barricade in Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was under the control of the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the intersection with the road to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This is a turnoff for the road to Veternica and this barricade was under the control of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is also stated here that joint control will be conducted by commanders of the HVO and the armed forces of Vitez in the presence of UNPROFOR, and representatives of the church and the Islamic religious community, the deadline being 1800 hours. Point 3 says that the regional HVO headquarters in Kruscica needs to be released, and all prisoners in the Lovac Motel should be released. So this is the HVO headquarters; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The commander of the armed forces also guarantees that barricades will not be put up again in the same area. That's what he means; doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but this decision was not respected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also, the commander of the HVO takes upon himself to consult with HVO commander for central Bosnia for the purpose of setting up a mixed commission of the HVO and the armed forces, which would establish the consequences of the conflict at the Plavac hotel. That hotel is also situated in Kruscica; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then paragraph 5 says that after the blockade has been lifted in Vitez, as well as the blockade of the regional HVO headquarters, the rear command of the armed forces captured by the HVO forces would be released. So the TO in the secondary school centre was under blockade too and that blockade had to be lifted?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are familiar with this event and the announcement?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It was published by the media and broadcast on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time the High Commissioner for Refugees' office was in Vitez; wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the High Commissioner for Refugees had their offices, and the British battalion was based in Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was the High Commissioner for Refugees based in Vitez, do you know?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The reason is clear, because there were a large number of people exiled by the Serb forces arriving in Vitez in the late autumn of 1992, and there were about 5,000 of these people, these exiles. They were mostly Bosniaks coming from Western Bosnia, and later on particularly from the area of Jajce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those Muslim refugees received by the Croatian authorities? Were any facilities provided for their accommodation?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that the humaneness we showed was of a high level. We saw them as poor people who had lost everything, who had been deprived of their homes and property. Many of them had been physically abused as well, and I think that all of us in Vitez, regardless of the ethnic group we belonged to, were willing to help as far as our possibilities allowed. Considerable assistance to the refugees, to the displaced people, were given by the official authorities who made available to them various facilities for their accommodation. By way of illustration, let me say that the kindergarten stopped working. This was one of the most attractive ones in Central Bosnia. It happens to be 20 or 30 metres from my home. Refugees from Prijedor were accommodated there, specifically a large Muslim village called Kozarac in Prijedor municipality, the entire population of which had been expelled and they found shelter in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the UNHCR leave Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If I remember well, they left after the fierce conflict that occurred in Busovaca. I think that that was when they left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or was it after these conflicts?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Let me correct myself. After the conflict that occurred on the 20th of October in Vitez and in Novi Travnik, the High Commissioner and the office of the UNHCR moved to Zenica, because their leaders claimed that the security situation was unreliable, there was repeated shooting, their vehicles had come under fire. However, the leaders of these two international institutions, the UNHCR and the High Commissioner stayed on to assist the growing number of displaced people coming to the Lasva Valley and Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this conflict on the 20th of October, 1992, do you know whether a coordination commission was formed to protect the interests of citizens and for what purpose?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Upon the initiative of citizens had who felt increasingly exposed in Stari Vitez, and when I say Stari Vitez I'm also implying the part of Stari Vitez known as Mahala and the other around the parish church, the Bosniak Muslims and Croats set up this coordination body for the protection of the interest of citizens. Heading that body upon the proposal of Muslims of that area, engineer Pavlovic, Luvomir Pavlovic, was elected. He was an influential and for our conditions a well-off citizen, a respected Croat, citizen and businessman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether that committee assisted in the reconstruction of destroyed houses in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that the conflict was very fierce, a number of houses were damaged, mostly Bosniak houses because most of the houses there were Bosniak, and the first task of that coordination body for the protection of citizens was to issue an appeal to the public and to institutions of the civilian government in Vitez, and people with means to collect funds and material assistance to repair the damages done in the conflict, and this applied to homes and business premises, and the response was beyond many expectations. A large number of people, and I must underline this, these were damaged Muslim houses, but a large number of Croat citizens whole-heartedly contributed to this collection campaign to repair those houses and a number of those houses were repaired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the help of those donations?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, Jajce fell on the 24th of October; didn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the fall of Jajce mean for the Lasva Valley in particular?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The fall of Jajce can be viewed from two standpoints, what it meant to the Croats and the population of Central Bosnia in general. First of all, it raised fears, because the road was open to the Serb forces, to Lasva and Central Bosnia. According to some indications, the Serbs were very keen to gain control of certain military installations in that area. I mean, Jajce, Novi Travnik and Vitez. Another aspect of the fall of Jajce was the large number of displaced people who arrived in the next two or three days, crossing the hills of Lasva and Travnik in the Lasva River Valley, many of them in Vitez itself. Among them, several thousand Croats and several thousand Muslims. The population composition in Jajce with respect to Croats and Muslims, I won't speak about the Serbs this time, who were numerous in Jajce, but the share of Muslims and Croats was roughly the same, so that there were a large number of displaced both Croats and Muslims. However, the Croats did not wish to stay in Vitez in the Lasva Valley under any circumstances. They had already experienced the horrors of war, and they knew or felt that those horrors would not bypass us, because the tension between the Croats and the Muslims had already reached a very high level, while at the same time the Serbs were nearby and they could already hit the Lasva Valley with heavy weapons. So this was the reason why the Croats used every effort, in spite of the efforts of the local authorities for them to stay, they wanted to live in the Lasva Valley and they most, in fact, did. I must say we wanted the able-bodied people to stay behind, those with weapons, with wartime experience, but they didn't want to and no one could keep them there. An enormous percentage, in fact, I could say more than 95 per cent of the Croats that came from Jajce left in the next couple of days, the region of Vitez and the Lasva Valley. Contrary to this, the Bosniaks, of course to their regret, had no where to go. The Croats did. They wanted to go to the south of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina where the Croats were in a majority. They were also received in Croatia itself, which Croats consider to be their motherland, whereas the Bosniaks stayed on in Central Bosnia and shared what little we had with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the fall of Jajce, the frontlines with the Serbs were more or less stabilised in the area where you were?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. When Jajce fell, a narrow corridor was captured linking Jajce to Travnik and the Lasva River Valley, and it was along this corridor that we sent units and material and humanitarian aid to Jajce. Armoured vehicles used this corridor to take the wounded. Even though Jajce had a high quality wartime hospital, the most serious cases needed to be taken further, and an improvised armoured vehicle was made out of a standard bus, and then our skilled workers covered this bus with heavy steel plate so that they couldn't be hit, and village roads were used at night without the lights being switched on. With the fall of Jajce this corridor was captured too, and the line was finally established between the Serbs and the HVO and the BH army forces, which was partly deployed within the territory of Travnik municipality, that is the area which was strategically dominant for Travnik and the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I now show you a map? It's in colour, so it's more easier to see the ethnic composition of the population in 1994, roughly at the time of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be marked D33/2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Could it be placed on the easel so that Mr. Cilic can point to it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a map from June 1993, but that was roughly the situation as it was in April. Mr. Cilic, the red areas, who do they belong to?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: These were areas under the control of the Serb forces, and on the other side as well. This is a well-known Serb stronghold, Ozien, which resisted for a long time all attempts by BH forces to capture it because it was a significant interest for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the green areas?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The green areas were controlled by the BH army forces or the Muslim forces. At the time we called them by different names, so when I say Muslim forces I am not using it in derogatory terms, it was simply the name that was used at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the blue area?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The blue area is the Lasva Valley that we're talking about. This is the Lepenica Valley, which covered three municipalities, Kiseljak, Kresevo and Fojnica, a part of Fojnica because most of Fojnica was under the Muslim forces. And this is a part, but I don't think that -- a part of Vares municipality under the control of the Croats, but in fact, it was much smaller than shown on the map. It is a part of the Vares plateau called Dastansko and the Croats remained in spite of being surrounded by Serbs and Muslims. But it was much smaller in area, with a far smaller population, because most of the Croats were exiled from the Vares municipality. And this is the Zepce area, which included in addition to Zepce itself, Maglaj, Zavidovici, so that it was a relatively large territory. It was known as Zepce though. It was larger than Zepce itself. And up there is Ursars, an area, one of the few, where the Muslims and Croats waged war together against the Serbs throughout. And the most serious problems between the Muslims and the Croats occurred only after the end of the war and those difficulties occurred at the political level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These areas, the Lasva and the Lepenica valleys, in fact, this was a unified area in January '93.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: After the conflict between the Muslims and the Croats on the 25th of January, 1993, and later on it was established that that was the aim of the Muslim forces, that is, to intersect the road at a distance of some 10 kilometres, and this remained until the end of the war, one can even say up to this day. Part of this territory is under Bosniak Muslim authority and the rest under Croatian authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where Kacuni and Bilalovac are?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Kacuni is right next to this area of Busovaca, so if you're going from the northwest eastwards, then after leaving Busovaca, two kilometres from there is Kacuni where the Muslim units were. It was a centre, which was quite a large centre, with a school, a health clinic, some small businesses, so that was where these units were based.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Bilalovac?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Bilalovac is, if you go on along the road towards Kiseljak, these areas are linked by the regional road, Sarajevo, Kiseljak, Busovaca, Kaonik, and then it forks off, one fork to Zenica and the other to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned Kacuni and Bilalovac and the road in Kacuni. When did the conflict occur there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that checkpoint -- there were numerous incidents before this, and I fear I won't be able to give the exact dates -- an assassination was attempted against high officials of the Croats, Ignac Kostroman and even Tihomir Blaskic, but things calmed down and the flow of traffic was resumed in spite of high risks until the conflict that occurred on the 25th of January, and I think that on the 26th or the 27th of January, the BH army definitely gained control of this territory of about 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was when this kind of ethnic structure was established?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, because this was very unfavourable for the Croats. The Lasva Valley was under total blockade; it didn't have communication with any other area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This 10-kilometre area that was captured by the BH army, what happened to the Croats in that part of the territory?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were, in fact, more Croats than Muslims living there, percentage-wise. However, in a very fierce conflict that lasted for two or three days in Busovaca municipality and which spread to some other areas as well, all the Croats from that region were expelled. I don't know whether it is of any interest for me to mention a figure referred to by a representative of the UNHCR and the High Commissioner for Refugees, that 277 Croatian homes were destroyed and 35 Bosnian homes. This is a figure of the International Community presented at a press conference in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is that area from Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The distance between the municipal centres is 12 or 13 kilometres, that is between Vitez and Busovaca. If we add to that another two and a half kilometres to Kacuni, then all in all the distance is about 15 kilometres between the centre of Vitez and Kacuni.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which villages were ethnically cleansed?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I couldn't list them. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the name Dusina mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Dusina is not on that main road. That is why I didn't mention it. But I do know everything about Dusina. Dusina is in the territory of Busovaca municipality at the point between three municipalities, and I assume that you want to ask me what happened in Dusina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, briefly.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 25th of January, the first large-scale crime occurred for the first time in the war between the Croats and Muslims. In a single day, on the 25th of January, the Muslim forces killed and massacred 14 captured soldiers and several civilians. According to some reliable estimates -- of course, not my own estimate which cannot be reliable or relevant -- this crime later on determined the course of the war which took the bloodiest possible turn in the Lasva River Valley. May I just add, unfortunately I had the occasion to see a video recording of the bodies of the people killed and massacred in Dusina because teams from Zenica managed to make this recording in the morgue of the Zenica hospital, and this video was shown at a press conference in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you said that this was the first big crime in the Muslim-Croat conflict in this area and wider, did this crime cause the Croatian population to be afraid?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course, it caused great fear among the population because people could read about it, hear about it on the radio, and even see it on television because the cruelty of it at that time was incomprehensible for us. Later on, we saw such atrocities, but at first, it was a great shock for everyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. We're moving on to 15 April, '93. Where were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: 15 April, 1993, is the day before the fierce conflict and war between the Croats and Muslims in the Lasva River Valley. I have to say that the day before -- of course, I was in the Vitez Brigade headquarters that night and on that morning, and the command post, the headquarters, was about 100 metres away from the command post of the operational zone of Central Bosnia. We were in the premises which was the Workers' University before, and the local media outlets were also located there, radio and television, that is. On that day, I received a task to go to a hastily organised press conference in Busovaca. Busovaca organised regular weekly press conferences, and they were usually held on Wednesday. However, this press conference was called for Thursday at 12.00. However, early in the morning we learned what it could have been about and what the reason could have been for calling this press conference. That morning, early in the morning, on the road which leads out of the town of Zenica, near the headquarters of the Jure Francetic Brigade, the escort of -- the commander of this Brigade, Zivko Totic, was killed in a very cruel way. Four bodyguards were killed by dozens of bullets, and in order to conceal this crime and its perpetrators, another passer-by was also killed, who was an ethnic Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: We have a videotape of several minutes and we have a transcript in English and in Croatian, and this is the videotape of this press conference in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The videotape is marked D34/2, the Croatian translation D34A/2, and the English D34B/2. (Videotape played) THE INTERPRETER (Voiceover): "Dear colleagues, ladies and gentlemen. "This is an emergency press conference called in connection with this morning's events which have happened in Zenica. "In the morning, around 8.00, in Podrezje, on the road near the brigade command post, the vehicle of the Commander of the Jure Francetic Brigade in Zenica was attacked. On that occasion, four persons were killed. The Commander escort: Ivica Vidovic, Anto Zrnic, Marko and Tihomir Ljubic and another person whose name is still not known. "According to the police report, it is probably an eyewitness to the event. "The brigade commander Zivko Totic was kidnapped and taken in an unknown direction. "Five persons were killed. "The colleagues from the HVO press from Zenica recorded it, so we can watch the film." "It is assumed that he was a witness to the accident." "The situation from February until the last incident. I list in order: "On 27th February, 1993, at a checkpoint between Vjetrenica-Maslinek, a part of goods from the Caritas convoy. "On 28th February, the car owned by Marinko Hrgic was taken from four persons by the BH army members in Zenica. Vukovic, member of the BH army, was arrested trying to break into an HVO vehicle. "On 17th March in Kakanj, a girl named Gordana Rados was seriously wounded. "On 23rd March, the BH army members shot from a truck at the military police building. "On 23rd March, the BH army members shot from the hospital using small arms at the military police building in Travnik. On the same day, the BH army members took down the Croatian flag and burnt it at the checkpoint Vilosten in Kakanj. "On 24th March, the Green Berets arrested two military policemen and held them in custody. "On 23rd March, the BH Army members threw a hand grenade at the HVO units location. "On 24th March, the BH army members shot at Croatian houses in Donja Veceriska. "On 25th March, the BH army members threw a hand grenade at the entrance of the St. Elias church. "On 7th April, members set an explosive device under the kiosk near the hotel 'Orient' in Travnik. On 25th March in Zenica, Father Stjepan Radic, the vicar of St. Elias church on --"

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: We can stop here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, this was the introductory part of this press conference. What happened subsequently?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In my opinion, the tone was regular, but the atmosphere at the premises where the press conference took place was very heavy. You cannot really get a good impression of what these bodies looked like, because the videotape is black and white and the videotape was colour. You could see traces of blood all over the car and in the surrounding area, and then this recitation of all the incidents which had taken place brought us back to all these events which we experienced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember of these incidents mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I believe we even mentioned some of them here. For instance, the Kruscica incident and the killing of Commander Stojak, and five or six additional incidents, I think, we covered earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Very well. I think this would be a good place to stop for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Have you got a few more questions for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Not a few more. One group. It's two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Two hours was suggested --

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What I tried to say yesterday, we have certain changes and certain witnesses are not coming, so Mr. Cilic is now testifying to some of the issues which would have been covered by some other witnesses. utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Tomorrow we will be sitting from 9.00 to 1.30, and then from 3.00 to 5.30, but there will be no sitting on Thursday, as you know. Mr. Terrier.
